calls.head: The Stars’ power play outclasses the Sabres’
calls.body: On the power play, Dallas is one of the league’s best, but Buffalo is near the bottom. Every penalty the Sabres take could cost them.
calls.call: The Stars’ power play creates more per 60 than the Sabres’.

calls.title: Dallas’ power play made more chances
calls.plain: The Stars came out clearly ahead on the power play, as the gap between these two suggested. On the scoreboard: Dallas 1 for 2, Buffalo 0 for 3 on the power play.
calls.said: the Stars’ power play would make more chances than the Sabres’
calls.beyond: Buffalo has a weaker power play than most, and Dallas has one of the league’s stingiest penalty kills. Even by those standards, this was a dry night: Buffalo’s power play created 2.0 expected goals per 60, against their usual 7.2 (about 6.5 against Dallas) and a league average of 7.6. A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

calls.head: Where the Stars have the edge: shots from defensemen
calls.body: The Stars are around the middle of the league for shots from defensemen, and the Sabres are near the bottom. That’s the biggest gap between these two, and it isn’t a big one.
calls.call: The Stars’ defensemen take a bigger share of the team’s shot attempts than the Sabres’.

surprises.head: A shutout for Jake Oettinger
surprises.body: Oettinger stopped all 26 shots, worth 2.3 expected goals. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 20 starts.

story.head: Nothing gets past Oettinger
paras: Jason Robertson struck first for the Stars midway through the first. Sam Steel, Mikko Rantanen and Roope Hintz scored three goals in just under six minutes midway through the second to stretch the lead to 4-0, and the Sabres never had an answer. Rantanen finished with four points on a goal and three assists, and Wyatt Johnston had three assists.

The chances were closer than the score. Jake Oettinger was perfect for the Stars, 26 saves on 26 shots, and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen stopped 14 of 18. The Stars improved to 2-2-0, sixth in the Central. The Sabres dropped to 2-2-0, slipping to sixth in the Atlantic.
